messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - Creates bla.ar containing test1.xml and test2.xml using ArArchiveOutputStream.
  - Opens that archive via ArArchiveInputStream and copies only the entry named "test1.xml" to a new archive bla2.ar; for all other entries it consumes their data (to advance the stream) but does not write them to the new archive.
  - Tracks how many entries were skipped (deleted) and asserts deleted == 1.

- Observed failure:
  - The loop relies on ArArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry() to iterate entries. The test expects two entries to be returned so that one can be deleted. Instead, only the first entry is returned; the second is never seen, so deleted remains 0 and the assertion fails.

- Why it happens:
  - In org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.ar.ArArchiveInputStream.getNextEntry() → getNextArEntry(), EOF is detected using input.available() == 0.
  - Using available() to detect end-of-file is incorrect. For buffered/file streams, available() can return 0 even when more data is available (e.g., after consuming the buffer between entries), causing a premature EOF signal.
  - As a result, after reading the first entry’s content, the subsequent call to getNextEntry() can return null even though the archive still contains more entries (like test2.xml), so the deletion loop stops too early.

- Relation to the bug report:
  - The report states that getNextEntry only delivers test1.xml, which “looks correct” to the caller, but an external ar -t still lists both test1.xml and test2.xml in the archive. This is consistent with the reader prematurely stopping due to the faulty available() check: the second entry isn’t surfaced by getNextEntry even though it is present in the file, which an external tool correctly shows.

- Conclusion (root cause):
  - Premature EOF detection in ArArchiveInputStream.getNextArEntry() due to using InputStream.available() to decide end-of-archive. The method should determine EOF by attempting to read the next header (or by checking actual read() return values), not by available().

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

I will now inspect the read methods in ArArchiveInputStream to confirm where EOF detection and reading are handled.
I must call exactly one tool per message and have already used a tool in this message. I will provide the final answer now.
